obstruction: A guaranteed source-disjoint projection batch is a strong independent set in the source-clause hypergraph. The all-input n/9 guarantee is tight, yet tightness does not imply decision hardness because the extremal family has a paid direct recognizer and explicit witness.
proof: A9 is the resolvable STS(9): every pair of variables occurs in exactly one source clause, so the primal graph is K9. In the cyclic lift, each layer is K9 except the two nonedges {p0,p1},{p0,p2}; a doubled layer must select p0 and one of p1,p2, and adjacent doubled layers conflict through the shifted clause. Hence doubled layers form an independent set of a cycle, giving at most floor(r/2), attained by alternating doubled layers and a safe singleton elsewhere.

recognition_escape.algorithm: authenticate canonical primal components; if every component is K9, solve each constant nine-variable component by at most 512 source evaluations and verify the joined source witness. Scrambled names, blocks, clauses and literal orders are allowed.
recognition_escape.decision: SAT without constructing any projection batch or using a SAT-label oracle
recognition_escape.peak: O(N) cached source/component map, or logarithmic live indices with paid repeated scans
recognition_escape.time: O(N log N) under sorting-based component acquisition plus at most 512 evaluations per nine-variable component, or polynomial repeated scans

theorem: The signed affine-plane A9 original is valid canonical, connected, SAT with 18 models, and has primal graph K9; hence its maximum source-disjoint pivot batch is one.
For t disjoint renamed A9 copies, alpha=t=n/9, so no all-input theorem can guarantee more than n/9 source-disjoint pivots.
For the prior connected affine incidence lift F_r, alpha=1 for r=1 and alpha=r+floor(r/2) for r>=2. Thus this connected family admits asymptotically n/6, but still only a linear one-phase batch.
